faq.title: Questions and answers
faq.contact: Can’t find your answer? Write to <email>general@genaifund.ai</email>.
faq.whoQ: Who can apply to a campaign?
faq.whoA: Anyone with a solution: solo builders, student teams, startups, software houses, agencies and enterprise teams. Each campaign lists its own eligibility.
faq.companyQ: Do I need a company to submit a proposal?
faq.companyA: No. You can apply as an individual or as a team, and add an organisation profile later if you want one.
faq.productQ: Do I need a finished product?
faq.productA: No. A working prototype helps, but a clear point of view on the problem and how you would solve it is enough to apply.
faq.reviewQ: How are proposals reviewed and shortlisted?
faq.reviewA: GenAI Fund screens every submission and invites a shortlist to present on demo day, where the enterprise and judges score live. Every applicant hears back.
faq.shortlistQ: What happens if we are shortlisted?
faq.shortlistA: You move into a scoped pilot with the enterprise. Selected teams can also be considered for investment, at the programme partners’ discretion.
faq.runsA: BeyondPilot is backed by GenAI Fund, the AI-focused fund connecting enterprises with AI builders across Southeast Asia.

question.label: The question
question.text: How might we make insurance in Vietnam something people are glad to hold — easy to buy, easy to carry, easy to claim?
question.setBy: Set by Tasco's leadership team, with GenAI Fund

teams.label: present live at demo day on 22 October

investment.label: investment considered for teams that come through the pilot

pilot.label: of pilot with the business owners who would run it

challenge.title: The challenge
challenge.lead: Compulsory motor insurance is something nearly every driver in Vietnam has to carry. It is mandated and priced by regulation, so every provider offers the same cover at the same price — and when a product is regulated into sameness, the experience around it stops improving.

paper.title: It's still paper
paper.text: Lose the paper and, in every way that matters, you've lost the policy.

must.title: People buy it because they must
must.text: A compliance purchase, with no relationship before or after the sale.

unaware.title: Few know what they're covered for
unaware.text: Most people find out the difference at the worst possible moment.

carry.title: You have to carry it, or pay
carry.text: If you can't produce it when you're stopped, you're fined.

same.title: Every product looks the same
same.text: Same cover and the same regulated price, right across the market.

claim.title: Claiming means a call and some hope
claim.text: Support runs through hotlines, and nobody can see where a claim stands.

constraint.title: One hard constraint
constraint.text: No premium discounts, cashback or disguised price incentives. The point is a better experience, not a bought outcome. Everything else is open.

who.title: Who can apply
who.lead: Judged on the solution, not the company. One person with a prototype and a software house with a product in market apply the same way.

win.title: No cash prize. A buyer instead.
win.lead: Most pilots die for one reason: the people in the room couldn't buy anything. This challenge fixes that part first.

yes.title: The people reviewing your work can say yes
yes.text: Tasco's leadership and the business owners who run its insurance operation set the brief, sit at demo day and choose what moves forward. The budget is allocated.

partner.title: A partner that has already done this
partner.text: In September 2026, Tasco led an investment round into BonBon, a startup it first met through its own innovation programme, with GenAI Fund investing alongside.

investment.title: Investment of up to US$100,000
investment.text: Teams that come through the pilot can be considered for investment, on top of the commercial relationship. Offered at the partners' discretion, after due diligence.

directions.title: Directions to build from
directions.lead: Eight places the experience breaks, in the order a customer meets them. Take one, combine several, or make a better case for your own.

buying.label: Buying
buying.lead: Getting covered should take minutes, not a call-back

carrying.label: Carrying
carrying.lead: The policy should be there when it's needed

claiming.label: Claiming
claiming.lead: The worst day should be the simplest part

d1.title: Frictionless purchase and renewal
d1.text: Buy, renew and pay without a queue, a call-back, or a form you fill in twice.

d2.title: Understand before you buy
d2.text: Explain cover in plain language, so people know what they're getting.

d3.title: The right cover for the right person
d3.text: Use consented data to fit protection to one driver, not an average one.

d4.title: Proof in your pocket
d4.text: Digital, instantly verifiable, impossible to lose or leave at home.

d5.title: Help that arrives first
d5.text: Renewal reminders and useful prompts that come before the problem does.

d6.title: Answers at the moment of need
d6.text: Support through chat, voice or in-app, without a hotline queue.

d7.title: Guided claims
d7.text: Tell people what's covered, what's needed, and where their claim stands.

d8.title: Faster assessment
d8.text: Close the gap between filing and resolution.

other.title: Something else entirely
other.text: Combine directions, or bring one nobody has thought of.

timeline.title: Timeline
timeline.lead: Three weeks, six fixed dates. The build period opens the same day as applications.

submit.title: What to submit
submit.lead: Make it tangible: show what improves for the customer, how it works, and what you'd need to test it for real.

framing.title: Problem framing
framing.text: Who you're helping and which friction you're solving.

prototype.title: Prototype or design
prototype.text: The proposed experience and how it works. A working prototype is preferred.

impact.title: Impact and assumptions
impact.text: The improvement you expect, and what you're assuming.

needs.title: Implementation needs
needs.text: Data, integrations and enterprise support required.

responsible.title: Responsible design
responsible.text: Data access, consent and privacy assumptions, and where staff review is needed.

roles.laura: CEO and Managing Partner, GenAI Fund
roles.rizwan: Partner, Positive Moves · Ex-Executive Director, EY
roles.hawkins: Director, Head of VNGGames Publishing Platform
roles.manuja: Head of AI and Data, Manulife

startup.q: Do I need to be a startup?
startup.a: No. Solo builders, student teams, startups, ISVs, systems integrators and enterprise teams can all apply. You're judged on the solution, not the company behind it.

inMarket.q: Can I apply with a product that's already in market?
inMarket.a: Yes — and those submissions often do well, because you can show something working on day one. Tell us what already exists and what you'd build or adapt for Tasco.

ip.a: You do. A mutual NDA is signed before any pilot begins. Commercial terms are agreed directly between you and Tasco, before work starts.

vietnam.q: Do I need to be in Vietnam, or speak Vietnamese?
vietnam.a: No. Applications, the briefing and demo day run in English, virtually. If you reach a pilot, you'll need people who can work with Tasco's team on Vietnam time.

hearBack.a: Submissions close 15 October at 23:59 ICT. On 16 October every applicant gets an outcome — shortlisted or not. Ten teams present live on 22 October, and pilot scoping starts on 23 October. No one is left waiting to find out by silence.

rail.note: You don't need a finished product to apply. You need a point of view and three weeks.
rail.hostText: Tasco runs automotive retail, VETC tolling, insurance and roadside assistance across Vietnam. GenAI Fund runs the programme and screens submissions.

closing.title: Ten teams present live on 22 October.
closing.text: Submissions close 15 October at 23:59 ICT. Everyone hears back on 16 October.
